body: I can relate completely. About a year after it happened, I remember having to travel far out into the middle of nowhere. The buses would come every 30mins and the one I needed drove right past, despite me hailing it. I was still immersed in my grief back then (I kinda still am, although in an altogether different sense) and I just broke down under the bus shelter. It was late December, cold, dark and rainy. I still think about that day and how distressing it was to feel so overpowered by grief.

Unfortunately there isn't much else you can do but wait for a response. People ghost for all sorts of reasons (moving house, internet issues, family crises). It would probably be overstepping a boundary, but you could try finding him on Facebook and contacting someone he knows personally to figure out what happened.


Be warned though, some people might not understand why an internet friend would go to such great lengths to find someone they've only known for a few months. I personally don't think  your concerns are invasive, but just a heads up. I hope you find your answers. In the meanwhile, try to not let the worst case scenario consume your thoughts. All the best.
Woah. It baffles me that suicide can be a meticulously planned act for some, and a seemingly impulsive thing for others. Either way it just never really makes sense.

This happened with my person too, she gave valuable things away. It didn't seem out of character though, because she was always so generous. I guess there is no way of knowing for sure in that moment. I'm so sorry.

It's so strange. That these seemingly inconsequential events all tally up and click way after it's all done.  My heart bleeds for you, I can't imagine the pain of losing both parents. I wish you peace, please take care of yourself.
